edges.evidence_label: Prospective cohort study

cut.label: dairy_intake -> insulin_igf1 (milk raises circulating IGF-1)
cut.reason: A 2009 systematic review (Qin et al., Int J Food Sci Nutr, DOI 10.1080/09637480903150114) reports RCTs found a WMD of 13.8 ng/mL (95% CI 6.1-21.5) for IGF-1 in milk-intervention groups, and this number is corroborated by multiple independent secondary sources - but the primary abstract was paywalled/blocked from automated retrieval (PubMed cookie wall, ResearchGate/Tandfonline access denied), so no literal verbatim sentence could be obtained from the primary source. Per the acceptance bar, an edge without a verified verbatim sentence does not ship, even though the underlying claim is plausibly correct.

cut.label: sugar_reduction -> insulin_igf1
cut.reason: No dedicated RCT or meta-analysis was found that isolates generic 'sugar reduction' as a distinct exposure from glycemic-load/carbohydrate modification (which is already captured by the low_gi_diet edges) or from fructose specifically (which has its own, narrower literature on hepatic vs peripheral insulin resistance). Treating it as a separate edge risked double-counting the low-GI diet finding under a different label or fabricating precision the literature does not support.

cut.label: curcumin phytosome (Meriva) -> hs_crp_il6, quantified
cut.reason: Multiple RCTs (e.g., Meriva-brand phytosomal curcumin trials) qualitatively report larger CRP reductions than unformulated curcumin, but no verbatim, quantified pooled result sentence could be retrieved within the research budget for this specific formulation as its own meta-analysis. The curcumin_piperine edges above already demonstrate formulation-dependence; phytosome-specific numbers are flagged as an open item rather than asserted from search-summary text alone.

cut.label: alcohol -> hs_crp_il6 (added candidate, not in original list)
cut.reason: Design spec section 4.2 flags alcohol as a high-leverage cross-tree behavior worth adding, but the CRP relationship in the literature is J/U-shaped (moderate intake associated with lower CRP than both abstention and heavy intake) and the evidence base is cross-sectional/cohort, not RCT (ethically, heavy drinking cannot be randomized long-term). The schema's single-direction (+/-/null) field cannot faithfully represent a non-monotonic dose-response without misleading simplification, so this was left out of Goal B rather than forced into a binary direction. Better suited to Goal C (sleep) where the REM-suppression literature is more directly dose-linear, if pursued separately.

cut.label: Ambient room temperature -> Sleep onset latency
cut.reason: Could not obtain a verbatim, numerically-quantified result sentence from a resolvable-DOI primary source directly linking ambient/bedroom temperature to sleep onset latency in minutes. The one systematic review located with a clean DOI (Bennett et al. 2024, Sleep Medicine Reviews, DOI 10.1016/j.smrv.2024.101915, 'A systematic review of ambient heat and sleep in a warming climate') confirms only a directional association ('higher outdoor or indoor temperatures are generally associated with degraded sleep quality and quantity') with no minute-level quantification in its abstract. Other specific numeric claims surfaced during search (e.g. '5C increase -> ~2 min SOL increase', '+0.04 min per degF from 3.75 million nights') traced only to secondary AI-generated summaries or an unpublished conference abstract (SLEEP supplement) without a verifiable, resolvable-DOI verbatim sentence backing the exact number. Per the no-assertion-from-memory rule, this edge is cut rather than shipped with an unverifiable number.

cut.label: coffee consumption -> LDL cholesterol, precisely quantified pooled effect size
cut.reason: The one available RCT meta-analysis (Jee et al. 2001, DOI 10.1093/aje/153.4.353) establishes a clear dose-response direction (unfiltered coffee raises LDL, filtered does not) but its abstract does not report a numeric pooled effect size, and the full text was not retrievable within the research budget. Shipped as a qualitative edge instead (direction with no numeric effect) rather than cut outright, per the rule that a qualitative, directionally-supported finding is acceptable when no number is available to misstate.

cut.label: aerobic exercise -> resting heart rate (quantified reduction), as its own dedicated edge
cut.reason: Training-induced bradycardia is well established physiologically, but the specific meta-analyses located within budget either did not report a clean pooled resting-HR number (a 2026 detraining meta-analysis reported resting HR as 'no longer significant' in the reversal/detraining direction, not the training direction) or were not accessed in time. The resting_hr_arterial_stiffness marker slot is instead filled by the sauna null-result edge; a dedicated quantified aerobic-exercise-to-resting-HR edge is a good candidate for a follow-up research pass.

cut.label: sleep duration (habitual, non-experimental) -> HbA1c/fasting glucose, dose-response meta-analysis
cut.reason: Multiple cohort studies link short habitual sleep to higher diabetes risk, but a quantified RCT or meta-analysis giving a specific HbA1c or fasting-glucose number tied to a specific sleep-duration change (rather than diabetes incidence risk ratios) was not located within the research budget. The sleep_restriction -> insulin_sensitivity_homa_ir edge (Donga 2010) covers the same underlying mechanism with a single well-controlled RCT instead.

cut.label: resistance training -> HbA1c / insulin sensitivity in type 2 diabetes
cut.reason: Multiple recent (2026) meta-analyses on this topic were identified in PubMed search results but not fetched and reviewed within the research budget after the edge list reached sufficient breadth across all seven target markers with aerobic exercise, weight loss, Mediterranean diet, and sleep restriction already covering the glycemic/insulin-sensitivity markers. Worth a follow-up pass given resistance training's inclusion in the confirmed behavior list.

cut.label: HIIT -> blood pressure, as a chronic training effect distinct from VO2max
cut.reason: HIIT is confirmed and well evidenced for VO2max (shipped above) but a dedicated chronic HIIT-training blood-pressure meta-analysis distinct from acute post-exercise hypotension studies was not located and fetched within the research budget; the blood_pressure marker is already well covered by aerobic exercise, resistance training, DASH, sodium reduction, alcohol reduction, and added sugar.

cut.label: vitamin D / zinc / magnesium supplementation -> any cardiometabolic marker
cut.reason: These behaviors belong to the Goal A (male vitality) and Goal C (sleep) candidate lists per the design spec's section 4.1, not the cardiometabolic marker set specified for this file, so no search was performed for them here.

cut.label: protein_intake -> lean_mass, distribution/timing across the day (e.g., 4x25g pattern) as its own behavior
cut.reason: No dedicated, adequately powered RCT or meta-analysis was found within the research budget that isolates meal-to-meal protein distribution as a body-composition outcome separable from total daily protein intake; the existing distribution literature (e.g., Areta et al. 2013) measures acute muscle protein synthesis, not fat mass/lean mass/strength changes over weeks-to-months, so it does not meet this project's outcome bar. Folded into the protein_intake behavior's dose_or_intensity field instead of a separate node.

cut.label: hmb -> lean_mass, older/sarcopenic adults (as a second, separate edge)
cut.reason: Multiple 2024-2025 meta-analyses (e.g. PMC12655442, PMC12003145) report modest/mixed effects of HMB on handgrip strength and physical-performance batteries in adults over 50, but conflicting reviews and no single verbatim-quotable pooled estimate specifically for appendicular or total lean mass was retrieved within the research budget for this pass; left out rather than asserted from search-summary text alone.

cut.label: caloric_deficit_magnitude -> resting metabolic rate (adaptive thermogenesis)
cut.reason: Background sources (e.g. a 2022 tissue-loss/metabolic-adaptation study in Int J Obes, and the classic Ballor & Poehlman exercise/diet-restriction meta-analysis) clearly describe RMR decline with caloric restriction, but full abstract text with a verbatim, quotable numeric RMR effect was not retrieved within the research budget for this session. This is flagged as the single most promising addition for a future pass, since it bears directly on the resting-metabolic-rate marker and the caloric_deficit_magnitude behavior already in this file.

cut.label: alcohol -> fat_mass and alcohol -> lean_mass (general, beyond visceral fat)
cut.reason: Alcohol's relationship with total fat mass and lean mass is confounded by total caloric intake and cannot be isolated with a randomized design (heavy, sustained drinking cannot be ethically randomized long-term); only the visceral-fat-specific, total-fat-mass-adjusted cohort finding (Chesters et al. 2026) was kept, because its adjustment for total fat mass isolates a body-fat-distribution effect rather than a generic caloric one.

cut.label: D-aspartic acid, Tribulus terrestris
cut.reason: These appear in the design document's Goal A (male vitality / testosterone) candidate list, not in this goal's (body composition and strength) candidate behaviors; out of scope for this file and not evaluated.

cut.label: resistance_training / creatine_monohydrate -> lean_mass and max_strength in general (young, non-aged) populations, as separate edges alongside the aged-specific ones
cut.reason: The literature for general/young populations is broadly consistent with (and larger in magnitude than) the aged-specific effects already included, but a second, non-overlapping verbatim-quotable meta-analysis was not pulled for this pass given the research budget; the aged-specific creatine finding and the mixed-age Lopez 2021 resistance-training finding were judged sufficient to establish both behaviors without duplicating the same claim twice.

cut.label: bilingualism_cognitive_reserve -> global_cognition_older (delay in dementia/symptom onset)
cut.reason: Evidence is observational/retrospective and framed as a delay in age-of-onset (Cohen's d = 0.32 for age-of-onset studies) rather than a score on a named instrument; prospective incidence-rate studies (the design least confounded by education/immigration/SES) show a much weaker, largely null effect (d = 0.10). Age-of-onset-delay framing structurally mirrors the 'years of life' mortality-style metric this design explicitly excludes, and no RCT is possible for a lifelong exposure like bilingualism, so the claim cannot be cleanly separated from cohort confounding (bilingual populations in these studies differ systematically in education and immigration history).

cut.label: omega3_supplementation -> global_cognition_older or processing_speed, using the 2025 dose-response meta-analysis (PMC12368174) showing broad positive effects
cut.reason: This more recent 58-RCT dose-response meta-analysis reports positive effects across multiple domains (perceptual speed, language, memory, visuospatial function, global cognition), which would directly contradict the shipped null edge (Cochrane 2012, MMSE, cognitively healthy older adults). Rather than shipping both and leaving the contradiction unresolved, the population-matched, instrument-named, healthy-older-adult-specific Cochrane null was kept because it isolates the exact population and instrument (MMSE) that the design's marker specifies; the broader dose-response review pools healthy and impaired populations and multiple cognitive tests without isolating a single clean healthy-adult claim in its abstract.

cut.label: acute_aerobic_exercise -> processing_speed or global cognition, using the individual-participant-data meta-analysis (Ishihara et al. 2021, PMID 34147558)
cut.reason: This IPD meta-analysis's abstract reports only a qualitative moderation pattern (pre-test performance moderates the after-effect of acute exercise) with no quantified effect size, so no number could be placed in the `effect` field without violating the requirement that every number in `effect` be derivable from the edge's own verbatim. Superseded here by Chang et al. 2012 and Ludyga et al. 2016, both of which report quantified Hedges' g values in their abstracts.

cut.label: caffeine -> working_memory or sustained_attention_rt in well-rested, non-sleep-deprived healthy adults (i.e., caffeine's 'baseline' effect outside of sleep loss)
cut.reason: The literature on caffeine in rested, habitual consumers is heavily confounded by reversal of overnight withdrawal (habitual drinkers test worse than their true baseline without their usual dose, so a 'benefit' partly reflects relief of withdrawal rather than net enhancement). No abstract-quantified meta-analysis isolating a clean non-deprived, non-habituated caffeine effect with a named instrument was retrieved within the research budget; only the sleep-restricted/deprived population edge (Frontiers 2026 military meta-analysis) is shipped, with this exact caveat given in its conditional_on field.

cut.label: creatine_monohydrate -> working_memory, using secondary/news coverage claiming 'creatine users performed better on working memory' (nutraingredients.com, bubsnaturals.com)
cut.reason: These are secondary/marketing summaries of the sleep-deprivation RCT (Gordji-Nejad et al.), but the PubMed abstract of that RCT itself names only 'logical and numerical tasks, language-related processing speed, and the Psychomotor Vigilance Test (PVT)' as outcomes -- it does not use the phrase 'working memory' or report a working-memory-specific statistic. Shipping a working-memory edge from this source would require citing a paraphrase rather than the source's own verbatim, which the acceptance bar disallows.

cut.label: Alcohol -> anxiety_symptoms
cut.reason: No meta-analysis was found within the research budget that reports a clean, quantified pooled effect size for alcohol/AUD on a named anxiety instrument (GAD-7/STAI/HAM-A) with a verbatim-derivable number; available hits were either off-topic (PTSD neuroimaging papers matched by keyword overlap) or lacked a quantified anxiety-specific estimate.

cut.label: D-aspartic acid / Tribulus terrestris (expected null)
cut.reason: Not part of this goal's candidate list (these were Goal A/testosterone candidates); no mood-specific trials of either were identified as worth pursuing under the mood/anxiety goal, so they were not investigated here.

cut.label: St John's wort -> anxiety_symptoms
cut.reason: The literature on Hypericum focuses almost exclusively on depression outcomes; no dedicated meta-analysis isolating an anxiety-symptom instrument for St John's wort (as opposed to depression trials that happen to report an anxiety subscale) was found.

cut.label: Aerobic/resistance exercise -> cortisol (diurnal slope)
cut.reason: Pascoe 2017 (DOI 10.1016/j.psyneuen.2017.08.008) reports yoga/MBSR practices were associated with 'reduced evening cortisol, waking cortisol' but gives no quantified effect size or CI in the abstract, so no verbatim-derivable number could be extracted; the cortisol marker is instead covered via the mindfulness-based-interventions behavior using Rogerson et al 2024, which does report a quantified estimate.

cut.label: Loneliness-reduction intervention (e.g. befriending, social prescribing) -> depressive_symptoms as an RCT effect
cut.reason: Search effort found only observational/longitudinal-cohort evidence for the loneliness-depression relationship (Mann et al 2022, used above); no RCT meta-analysis of a loneliness-reduction intervention with a quantified depressive-symptom effect size was located within the research budget, so the behavior is represented only via the risk-factor direction, not an interventional reversal.

cut.label: Time in nature -> cortisol
cut.reason: Candidate searches for nature exposure and cortisol/HPA-axis outcomes returned disaster-exposure and natural-hazard mental health reviews (keyword collision on 'nature') rather than green-space/forest-bathing cortisol trials with a quantified pooled estimate; not pursued further given time budget.

cut.label: smoking_and_cessation -> cardiovascular_mortality and smoking_and_cessation -> cancer_incidence_mortality, cause-specific quantified
cut.reason: Jha 2013 (used for the all-cause mortality edges) reports only an all-cause hazard ratio in its abstract, not cause-specific breakdowns; other candidate papers found (Wang 2021 on cessation/weight-gain/CVD, Chang 2021 on smoking reduction) report CVD- or cancer-specific relative risks for narrower sub-questions (post-cessation weight gain, partial reduction rather than full cessation) that do not cleanly map to a general smoking-vs-never-smoking comparison for these two markers within the research budget.

cut.label: cardiorespiratory_fitness -> cardiovascular_mortality, quantified
cut.reason: The main available meta-analysis (Kodama 2009) pools CHD/CVD 'events' rather than cardiovascular deaths specifically, mixing fatal and non-fatal outcomes; assigning its RR (0.85 per 1-MET) to a cardiovascular-mortality-specific marker would misrepresent non-fatal events as deaths, so only the paper's all-cause mortality figure was kept.

cut.label: obesity_bmi -> cardiovascular_mortality, quantified
cut.reason: The Global BMI Mortality Collaboration's headline dose-response figures are for all-cause mortality; no BMI-specific, cleanly quotable cardiovascular-mortality dose-response estimate independent of the all-cause figures already used was retrieved within the research budget.

cut.label: central adiposity / waist circumference as a separate behavior from BMI
cut.reason: A strong dose-response meta-analysis exists (Jayedi 2020, BMJ, waist circumference HR 1.11 per 10cm), but it was not on the candidate behavior list and measures a distinct exposure (central fat distribution) from the requested 'obesity/BMI' behavior; adding it as its own node risked fragmenting the same underlying adiposity concept across two behavior nodes rather than clarifying it.

cut.label: air_pollution_pm25 -> cancer_incidence_mortality, direct PM2.5 (not NO2 proxy) dose-response for lung cancer specifically
cut.reason: A dedicated, cleanly quotable pooled PM2.5-to-lung-cancer dose-response meta-analysis (as distinct from the NO2/traffic-proxy meta-analysis actually used, or the gastrointestinal-cancer PM2.5 meta-analysis found) could not be retrieved within the research budget; the NO2/traffic-proxy edge was shipped instead with an explicit caveat rather than omitting the cancer marker for this behavior entirely.

cut.label: physical activity volume -> cancer_incidence_mortality, quantified
cut.reason: Arem 2015 (JAMA Intern Med, pooled leisure-time physical activity) states in its abstract that 'a similar dose-response relationship was observed for mortality due to cardiovascular disease and to cancer' but does not give a quotable, cancer-specific numeric hazard ratio in the abstract text itself; using it would have required paraphrasing a number not actually present in the verbatim, which the acceptance bar for this file does not allow.
